issues.legal_issue: An enforceable agreement to sell a residential capital asset may constitute a transfer of rights for determining whether a replacement home was purchased within the period for residential reinvestment relief, even if a court order prevents completion of the sale deed until later.
material_facts: The taxpayers entered into an agreement to sell their residential property and received earnest money from the buyer.
The agreement gave the buyer a right to seek specific performance, restricting the taxpayers from lawfully selling the property to someone else.
The taxpayers purchased another residential home within one year of the agreement and used the capital gain for that purchase.

A court order restraining the taxpayers from dealing with the property prevented execution of the sale deed until after the replacement home had been purchased; the restraint was later lifted and the sale deed was executed.
The proposed sale was not abandoned or neutralized by a later agreement or conduct.
issues.conclusion: The agreement to sell transferred rights in the original residential property for this purpose. The taxpayers were entitled to residential reinvestment relief, subject to fulfilment of the other applicable conditions, and the assessment decisions denying the relief were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied Section 2(47) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, under which transfer includes the extinguishment of rights in a capital asset, together with Section 54, which provides relief when a replacement residential house is purchased within the prescribed period. Although an agreement to sell does not ordinarily amount to sale of the entire property, an agreement that creates an enforceable right in the buyer and correspondingly extinguishes rights of the seller can amount to a transfer. The court interpreted these provisions purposively to advance the relief intended by Section 54, relying on Oxford University Press v. Commissioner of Income Tax (2001) 3 SCC 359, which supports purposive and harmonious interpretation in considering tax relief.

rule.if: capital_gains_tax_appeal and residential_asset_sold and enforceable_sale_agreement and buyer_paid_earnest_money and seller_rights_restricted_by_agreement and replacement_home_bought_within_one_year_of_agreement and capital_gain_used_for_replacement_home and court_order_prevented_prompt_sale_deed and sale_not_abandoned_or_neutralized

predicates.capital_gains_tax_appeal: The proceeding concerns whether a taxpayer is entitled to relief from tax on capital gain arising from the transfer of a residential asset.
predicates.residential_asset_sold: The taxpayer transferred a residential asset that generated a capital gain.
predicates.enforceable_sale_agreement: The taxpayer made an agreement to sell the asset that gave the proposed buyer an enforceable right to seek completion of the sale.
predicates.buyer_paid_earnest_money: The proposed buyer paid earnest money under the sale agreement.
predicates.seller_rights_restricted_by_agreement: The agreement restricted the taxpayer from lawfully selling the asset to another person while the buyer's rights remained in place.
predicates.replacement_home_bought_within_one_year_: The taxpayer bought a replacement residential home within one year after making the sale agreement.
predicates.capital_gain_used_for_replacement_home: The taxpayer used the capital gain from the transferred asset to buy the replacement home.
predicates.court_order_prevented_prompt_sale_deed: A court order prevented the taxpayer from completing the sale by executing the sale deed at the time contemplated by the agreement.
predicates.sale_not_abandoned_or_neutralized: The proposed sale was not abandoned or neutralized by a later agreement or by the parties' subsequent conduct.
predicates.taxpayer_entitled_to_residential_reinves: The taxpayer qualifies for relief from tax on the capital gain by reason of the replacement residential home purchase, subject to other applicable conditions.

issues.definition: When a taxpayer's enforceable agreement to sell a residential asset restricts the taxpayer's rights, the taxpayer buys a replacement home within one year and uses the gain for that purchase, and a court order delays completion without the sale being abandoned or neutralized, the taxpayer is entitled to residential reinvestment relief, subject to other applicable conditions.
